:::{#exm-huffman-optimal}
#### Three prefix codes for one source

<!-- no-figure: the example compares three expected lengths in a table -->

Take the source of @exm-huffman-code,
with [probabilities](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-probability) $(0.4, 0.2, 0.2, 0.1, 0.1)$.
Its [Huffman code](#def-huffman-code) has the [codeword length](source-coding.qmd#def-code)s $(2, 2, 2, 3, 3)$.
A fixed-length code gives every value three [bit](entropy.qmd#def-bit)s.
Giving each value $x$ the length $\ceil{-\log_2 \pf{x}}$ is a third choice of lengths.
All three choices satisfy the sum in @thm-kraft-inequality,
so @thm-kraft-converse gives a [prefix code](#def-prefix-code) for each.
The code below computes their [expected length](source-coding.qmd#def-expected-length)s.

```{r}
#| label: huffman-optimal-comparison
p <- c(0.4, 0.2, 0.2, 0.1, 0.1)
huffman_lengths <- c(2, 2, 2, 3, 3)
fixed_lengths <- rep(3, length(p))
shannon_lengths <- ceiling(-log2(p))
length_sets <- list(huffman_lengths, fixed_lengths, shannon_lengths)
data.frame(
  code = c("Huffman", "fixed length", "Shannon lengths"),
  kraft_sum = vapply(length_sets, function(l) sum(2^(-l)), numeric(1)),
  expected_length = vapply(length_sets, function(l) sum(p * l), numeric(1))
)
```

The Huffman code has the least expected length of the three,
as @thm-huffman-optimal says it must have among all prefix codes.

:::
